primitives.name: Passer Efficiency
primitives.verbatim_quote: A good forward passer at times becomes so efficient that it is extremely difficult for the very best defense to prevent him from accomplishing the pass.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'η_p': 'dimensionless efficiency ratio of passer success rate'}
primitives.assumptions: Passer efficiency η_p is a function of skill, situational awareness, and defensive pressure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When η_p approaches 1, defensive entropy minimizes; failure occurs when η_p < threshold.

layer2.mapping: Passer efficiency maps to signal-to-noise ratio in GSI's probabilistic model; in GSE, it governs action-state transitions.
layer2.telemetry: Success rate of completed passes under defensive pressure

primitives.name: Individual Performance
primitives.verbatim_quote: The essence of the forward pass is a high-class individual performance.
primitives.assumptions: Performance P_i is a composite of technical precision, timing, and decision-making.
primitives.breakdown_regime: P_i diverges from baseline when external constraints exceed internal capacity.

layer2.mapping: Individual performance kernel drives GSI's player evaluation tensor; in GSE, it defines agent behavior policy.
layer2.telemetry: Player-specific metrics of execution consistency and adaptability

primitives.name: Training Duration
primitives.verbatim_quote: It is extremely difficult to train a successful forward passer in one season.
primitives.assumptions: Training time T is inversely correlated with skill acquisition rate α.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Skill acquisition converges asymptotically as T → ∞; insufficient T leads to suboptimal η_p.

layer2.mapping: Training duration maps to learning curve in GSI's temporal inference engine; in GSE, it influences policy convergence.
layer2.telemetry: Time required to reach proficiency threshold for passer skill

Training duration T inversely affects skill acquisition rate α, such that longer T improves η_p. The system exhibits a dual nature: individual excellence (P_i) and collective constraint (H_d), where failure occurs when P_i < α(T) × H_d.
